text:
Let the soul plunge for an instant
into the arid sea of desire
and let your bronze effigy
rise, false, from its foam.


*


Let the breeze, in its breath, stir
your black, loose hair
and, wrapped in its caress,
the mist of your body.


*


To the white bowl of your soft hands,
feverish support for my burning brow,
to the red gleam of your fine lips,
sweet caress of my clumsy mouth,
always dreamed.


You who spill a curl over your brow
when your head bends sadly,
you who frighten in your black eyes
the melancholy light and sweet shine,
you who widen a sob in your neck
and moisten a sigh on your lips.


*


A synchrony of soft sighs,
savory with brine, dyed by the sun,
molded in the brown flesh
of the virgin of the sweet
and pastoral arpeggio.



1942

translation.title: Fossils
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish rendering. The sensual apostrophe, asterisks, and closing date are preserved; ‘resol’ is rendered as sunlight on the brine-colored flesh.
